description: Algorithmic CV sequencer: it walks a circular orbit through a field of two-dimensional noise, samples that orbit at a chosen number of points, and plays those points as steps whenever it is clocked

params.text: Sets which steps are taken off the main output and sent to the filtered one, 1 to 16 of them; the middle of its travel takes none and the two sides pick opposite sets of steps
Sets how many points the orbit is sampled at, 2 to 16; it does not shorten the sequence but samples the same circle more or less finely, so a change alters every step
Sets where in the noise field the orbit is centred, 1 to 10; moving it gives an entirely different sequence, and the module recalculates every step when it changes
Sets how wide the orbit is, 1 to 10, doubling the radius for every 1 it adds: at the bottom every step is nearly the same value, at the top they cover the field
Sets how far each step slides away from its noise value as the orbit creeps round, forward above the centre and backwards below; centred, nothing drifts
Sets the voltage the noise range is spread over, 0 to 5; it comes up at 0, which silences all three CV outputs until it is raised
Multiplies the rate at which the orbit creeps round, 1 to 10
Rotates the Euclidean filter pattern around the sequence; it is held below the step count, and it does nothing while the filter style is on ALG
Chooses how the drift is spread across the steps, printing Sphere, Hemisphere and Flat; on Flat every step moves together, and the other two add a sine offset that grows across the sequence
Chooses the range the outputs are mapped into, printing -5V to +5V, 0V to +10V and 0V to +5V
Chooses how the filter picks steps, printing Euclidean for an evenly spread pattern and Noise Algo for a pick made from each step's own value
Turns the sign of every step's noise value over, and the lamp is lit while that is on

inputs.text: A trigger moves the sequence on one step and it wraps round to the first after the last; it fires above 2V and rearms below 0.01V
A trigger sends the sequence back to its first step; it fires above 2V and rearms below 0.01V
Takes the BASE slider over while a cable is in it: 1V to 10V sets the value directly, the slider is dragged to match and cannot be moved by hand
Takes the RANGE slider over while a cable is in it: 1V to 10V sets the value directly, the slider is dragged to match and cannot be moved by hand
Takes the DRIFT slider over while a cable is in it: 0 to 10V is spread across the whole travel, so 5V is the centre, and the slider is dragged to match
Takes the AMP slider over while a cable is in it: 0 to 10V spans the whole travel, and the slider is dragged to match
Takes the FILTER slider over while a cable is in it: 0 to 10V is spread across the whole travel, so 5V is the centre, and the slider is dragged to match

outputs.text: Holds the voltage of the last step that the filter left alone, until the next such step
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step that the filter leaves alone
Holds the voltage of the last step the filter took, until the next such step
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step that the filter takes
Holds the voltage of the sequence's first step, refreshed each time the sequence comes round to it
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequence comes round to its first step

notes: AMP comes up at 0 and every step's voltage is multiplied by it, so a newly placed module puts out 0V on all three CV jacks until AMP is raised
the module has no clock of its own: nothing moves until a trigger arrives at TRIG IN
INVERT comes up on. The button rests at a value the module reads as a press on its first sample, so a newly placed module has the lamp lit and every step's sign turned over; one press clears it
a cable in any of the five CV jacks takes that slider over: the voltage is written into the parameter, so the slider moves on its own and ignores the mouse until the cable comes out
a step whose voltage would pass ±5V is folded back rather than clipped, so turning AMP up past the point where the noise reaches the rails bends the shape instead of flattening it
the steps are only recalculated when BASE, RANGE or STEPS change, and that is the costly part of the module; driving BASE or RANGE from an LFO makes it work far harder
the screen draws the whole sequence as a row of steps with the current one marked, showing the voltages after drift and AMP, so it moves as the orbit creeps even between triggers
menu: Drift Main Steps — lets the drift move the steps the filter leaves alone; it is on
Drift Filtered Steps — lets the drift move the steps the filter takes; it is on
Drift Drone — lets the drift move the drone step; it is on
Reset also resets Drift — makes a trigger at RESET IN put the orbit's creep back to where it started as well as the step counter; it is off
